# 📊 NBFC Daily Watch — Monday, November 16, 2026

Morning edition for Monday, 16 November 2026 (IST). Covers Friday evening to Sunday, 13–15 Nov. No market session since Friday: stock and index figures are Friday 13 Nov NSE closes, and IBJA's latest rates are Friday 13 Nov (PM). Monday's IBJA AM rates were not yet up at writing time.

## 🔴 URGENT / High Impact

### Muthoot Fincorp Q2 FY27: profit doubles to ₹779 crore, Stage III at 1.07%
Muthoot Fincorp's board approved its unaudited standalone results on Saturday 14 Nov and filed them with BSE that evening: Q2 FY27 profit was ₹779.41 crore against ₹388.31 crore a year earlier and ₹705.48 crore in Q1, on total income of ₹3,408.34 crore (up 70.7% year on year). Loans stood at ₹54,685.50 crore on 30 September, up 19.3% from 31 March, with Stage III at 1.07% of gross loans, net Stage III at 0.63%, provision coverage at 42.01% and capital adequacy at 19.38%.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the gross Stage III ratio sits well below the latest standalone prints of Manappuram (1.8%) and Muthoot Finance (3.87%), while impairment charges rose to ₹183.00 crore from ₹106.21 crore a year ago and ₹93.81 crore in Q1, and finance costs rose 68.7% to ₹1,161.53 crore. The same board meeting recommended converting 40 crore compulsorily convertible cumulative preference shares (CCCPS) into equity and reappointing Thomas John Muthoot, Thomas George Muthoot and Thomas Muthoot for five years from 1 February 2027, all subject to shareholder approval.
Sources: [BSE: board outcome and Q2 results, 14 Nov](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachLive/1b013a70-8ca6-4aff-ae25-9ef12e008024.pdf) · [Economic Times](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/ipo-bound-muthoot-fincorp-doubles-q2-profit-to-rs-779-crore-bucks-trend-of-rising-bad-loans/articleshow/135851622.cms) · [Business Standard: Manappuram Q2](https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/manappuram-finance-shares-dip-4-even-as-brokerages-upbeat-here-s-why-126111300542_1.html) · [Economic Times: Muthoot Finance Q2](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/earnings/muthoot-finance-q2-cons-profit-jumps-36-yoy-to-rs-3278-crore/articleshow/135401237.cms)

### RBI deputy governor rules out easing the 50% FOIR cap for microfinance
In a speech at an MFIN event in Mumbai on 13 Nov, published by RBI on 15 Nov, Deputy Governor Shirish Chandra Murmu turned down the industry's request to count only the interest part of some loans in the 50% repayment-to-income (FOIR) cap, saying it would "tinker with the sanctity of the limit and understate household leverage". He said RBI would review the ₹3 lakh household-income threshold, flagged rising microfinance lending rates and ticket sizes, and said credit bureaus have been told to move microfinance loans out of the consumer segment.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the cap governs Muthoot Microfin's book and any microfinance-type lending in the group, so there is no relief on household indebtedness limits. The bureau clean-up means microfinance loans reported under the consumer segment will start showing up in microfinance FOIR checks.
Sources: [RBI speech, 13 Nov 2026](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_SpeechesView.aspx?Id=1590) · [Economic Times](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/rbi-pushes-back-on-easing-microfinance-foir-flags-rising-rates-and-debt-risks/articleshow/135856447.cms) · [BusinessLine](https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/money-and-banking/mfis-should-lend-responsibly-as-climate-risks-could-impact-borrowers-rbi-deputy-governor/article71705221.ece)

Muthoot Microfin's board meets on Thursday 19 Nov to approve audited half-year accounts "for the preparation of restated consolidated financial statements" of Muthoot Fincorp ([NSE](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/muthootmicrofin_13112026182612_PriorintimationBoardMeeting19112026SD.pdf)). Muthoot Microfin also published newspaper notices of its postal ballot on 14 Nov; remote e-voting closes on 13 Dec ([BSE](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachLive/84d85152-7831-4995-9352-0852ab775660.pdf)).

## 📈 Market & Stock Summary

The last NSE closes (13 Nov) are in Key numbers below: Nifty 50 at 25,144.30, Nifty Financial Services at 27,855.50, Muthoot Finance at ₹2,840.00 and Manappuram at ₹308.00 ([NSE index closes](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/content/indices/ind_close_all_13112026.csv) · [NSE bhavcopy](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/products/content/sec_bhavdata_full_13112026.csv)).

### Update: Gold steadies near $3,892 on Monday; AGLOC's ₹10,574 ceiling ends today
Reuters had spot gold up 0.3% at $3,892.42 an ounce at 06:20 IST on Monday, after a 4.5% fall last week, as markets price a 94% chance of a 25-basis-point Fed hike in December. AGLOC's 85% ceiling of ₹10,574 a gram, on a jewellery reference of ₹12,440, covers 14–16 Nov, so a new period is due from Tuesday; IBJA's latest print is still Friday's ₹13,580.9 a gram for 999 (PM).
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the per-gram ceiling for fresh loans changes from Tuesday with AGLOC's next period, and it will be set off a domestic price that hasn't been printed since Friday's fall.
Sources: [AGLOC](https://www.agloc.org/) · [IBJA](https://ibjarates.com/) · [Mint (Reuters), 16 Nov](https://www.livemint.com/market/gold-edges-higher-as-investors-await-warsh-remarks-for-rate-signals-11794792432423.html)

## 🏛️ RBI & Regulatory — Headlines Only

No new RBI circular, notification or Master Direction for NBFCs since Friday: RBI's press releases end at 13 Nov items and its notifications at the 11 Nov Domestic Money Transfer Directions. SEBI's circulars page ends at 11 Nov, and its only weekend release is the IITF pavilion notice. The RBI deputy governor's microfinance speech is the second card above ([RBI press releases](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx) · [RBI notifications](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx)). Deep dive in NBFC Guru's 7 AM report.

## 💰 Financial Results & Performance

Muthoot Fincorp's Q2 is the lead story above. No listed peer filed results over the weekend.

### Update: NBFCs flag 5–15 bps more on funding costs after October's repo hike
ETBFSI's review of Q2 commentary says Aditya Birla Finance expects incremental borrowing costs to rise another 5–10 bps in Q3 and Cholamandalam guides for a 10–15 bps rise for FY27, while Bajaj Finance's CFO flagged a marginal extra margin headwind. Muthoot Finance put its cost of borrowing at about 8.6% on 30 September, with CFO Oommen Mammen saying other issuers were raising bonds at 8.3–8.4%, against about 7.5% earlier.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: Muthoot Fincorp's own Q2 finance costs rose 68.7% year on year to ₹1,161.53 crore, ahead of its 19.3% loan growth since March, so the repo hike's pass-through to fresh NCDs and bank lines is the margin line to watch in H2.
Sources: [ETBFSI](https://bfsi.economictimes.indiatimes.com/articles/nbfcs-see-up-to-15-bps-rise-in-cost-of-funds-as-rbi-rate-hike-feeds-through/135865369) · [BSE: Muthoot Fincorp Q2 results](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachLive/1b013a70-8ca6-4aff-ae25-9ef12e008024.pdf)

## ⚠️ Credit Rating Actions

### India Ratings affirms IIFL Finance at IND AA/Stable
IIFL Finance told the exchanges on 13 Nov that India Ratings affirmed IND AA/Stable on its NCDs, subordinated debt and bank loans and IND AA-/Stable on its perpetual debt. The agency also affirmed IND AA/Stable on the NCDs of subsidiaries IIFL Home Finance and IIFL Samasta Finance.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: IIFL Finance, a gold-loan peer, now sits at the same AA level as Muthoot Fincorp's CRISIL rating, as both compete for retail and institutional NCD money this quarter.
Sources: [NSE: IIFL Finance rating intimation](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/IIFL_13112026144720_SEIntimation_IndiaRatings.pdf)

## 🔄 Deals & M&A

### Sammaan Capital to enter gold loans in 16 branches this quarter
IHC-backed Sammaan Capital will soft-launch gold loans in about 16 branches in Q3 FY27 and another 30 in Q4, with an indicative ticket of about ₹2 lakh, yields of 11–13%, tenures up to three years and LTV up to 85% below ₹2.5 lakh, its management said on the Q2 call. It joins Tata Capital, Aditya Birla Finance and Godrej Finance among large diversified lenders moving into gold loans.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: one more well-funded entrant in Muthoot Fincorp's core product, though its chief operating officer said gold branches take 12–18 months to break even, so the competitive effect is slow.
Sources: [ETBFSI](https://bfsi.economictimes.indiatimes.com/articles/sammaan-capital-joins-gold-loan-push-by-large-nbfcs-to-launch-in-16-branches-in-q3/135864465) · [Business Standard: Aditya Birla Capital gold branches](https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/aditya-birla-capital-opens-100th-gold-loan-branch-eyes-1-000-outlets-126111201136_1.html)

## 💻 Digital & Fintech

No significant developments today.

## 📉 NPA & Asset Quality

Muthoot Fincorp's 1.07% Stage III ratio (lead story) is the weekend's only new asset-quality disclosure among gold lenders. ET's 14 Nov report on peers' Stage 2 rise on short-tenure and EMI gold loans was covered on 15 Nov.

## 👤 Personnel & Leadership

Muthoot Fincorp's board recommended five-year reappointments of Thomas John Muthoot (Managing Director) and Thomas George Muthoot and Thomas Muthoot (Joint Managing Directors) from 1 February 2027, subject to shareholder approval ([BSE](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachLive/1b013a70-8ca6-4aff-ae25-9ef12e008024.pdf)).

## 🏘️ Sector Deep Dive — Monday: Microfinance & SHG lending

**Where the sector stands.** Sa-Dhan's CEO Jiji Mammen says the microfinance portfolio fell to ₹3.3 lakh crore from ₹4.4 lakh crore before growth turned in March 2026 after about eight quarters of contraction, and he expects 10–15% growth this year, mostly in the second half ([Financial Express](https://www.financialexpress.com/money/mutual-funds-we-are-piloting-mutual-fund-distribution-through-mfis-sa-dhan-ceo-4378955/)). Sa-Dhan and AMFI are piloting mutual-fund distribution through MFIs in 10 states.

**What RBI said.** Deputy Governor Murmu's 13 Nov speech kept the two guardrails, the ₹3 lakh income ceiling (under review) and the 50% FOIR cap (not to be eased), and cited a study finding the average borrower spends 18.7% of monthly household income on repayments ([RBI](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_SpeechesView.aspx?Id=1590)). He named three problems, over-indebtedness, high rates and harsh recovery, and said lending rates are moving up across all types of lenders, partly on higher credit costs. Credit bureaus have been told to disable microfinance reporting in the consumer segment and migrate those records, and the bureaus have built Grameen Credit Score models for rural borrowers.

**What it means for Muthoot Fincorp's group.** Muthoot Microfin, the group's listed microfinance arm, works under the same caps; its board meets on 19 Nov on audited half-year accounts for Muthoot Fincorp's restated consolidated statements ([NSE](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/muthootmicrofin_13112026182612_PriorintimationBoardMeeting19112026SD.pdf)). The bureau migration matters most for borrowers who hold both a microfinance loan and a small gold loan, the overlap the gold lenders' own Stage 2 data has started to show.

# 📋 NBFC Regulatory Daily Report
**Date:** Monday, 16 November 2026 (IST)

---

## 🔔 New Regulatory Updates Today

No new regulatory developments today. Nothing came out between Friday evening and Sunday from RBI, SEBI, IBBI, NHB or FIU-IND for NBFCs, and nothing addressed to banks changes NBFC funding, risk weights, co-lending or gold loans.

### Watchlist sweep: nothing new for NBFCs over the weekend of 14–15 Nov
RBI's press-release feed still ends at its 13 Nov items (state and T-bill auctions, September balance of payments, the Mobikwik penalty, scheduled banks' position) and its notifications feed at the 11 Nov Domestic Money Transfer Directions. SEBI's circulars page ends at the 11 Nov FATCA/CRS circular, and its press releases at a 15 Nov notice on its IITF pavilion; IBBI's what's-new page showed no item dated 13–16 Nov.

# 📋 NBFC Weekly Analysis: Week of 9 – 15 November 2026

*Published Monday, 16 November 2026 (IST). Covers trading sessions Mon 9 and Wed 11 to Fri 13 November (Tue 10 Nov was an exchange holiday) and weekend news to Sunday 15 November. Muthoot Fincorp Ltd is a Middle Layer NBFC with unlisted equity and listed NCDs. Muthoot Finance Ltd is a separate, listed company; none of its numbers are Muthoot Fincorp's. Muthoot Capital Services is a separate listed group company, and Muthoot Microfin is a listed Muthoot Fincorp subsidiary.*

## Executive Summary

- **Muthoot Fincorp's Q2 profit doubled, and its Stage III ratio is low but up on the quarter.** Muthoot Fincorp's board approved standalone Q2 FY27 results on Sat 14 Nov and filed them on BSE: profit ₹779.41 cr (₹705.48 cr in Q1), loans ₹54,685.50 cr (+19.3% since March), Stage III 1.07%, net Stage III 0.63% and CRAR 19.38% ([BSE filing](https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachLive/1b013a70-8ca6-4aff-ae25-9ef12e008024.pdf)). ET puts year-ago profit at ₹388 cr and year-ago GNPA at 1.41%, with provisions up to ₹183 cr from ₹106 cr ([Economic Times](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/banking/finance/ipo-bound-muthoot-fincorp-doubles-q2-profit-to-rs-779-crore-bucks-trend-of-rising-bad-loans/articleshow/135851622.cms)). CARE's October rationale had standalone GNPA at 0.77% on 30 June, so Stage III rose about 30 bps in the quarter ([CARE Ratings](https://www.careratings.com/upload/CompanyFiles/PR/202610121058_Muthoot_Fincorp_Limited.pdf)). At 06:50 IST today the results were still not on the company's own investor page ([Muthoot Fincorp investors](https://www.muthootfincorp.com/investors)).
- **Gold-loan asset quality is now the sector story.** Muthoot Finance reported standalone Stage 2 of ₹23,467 cr at September-end against ₹1,876 cr in June, and Manappuram's gold Stage 2 rose to about 5% of the book; both blame monthly-interest and EMI products launched under RBI's April 2026 gold rules ([Economic Times](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/satet-front/dodging-bullet-loans-hurt-gold-nbfcs/articleshow/135817183.cms)). Bureau data put 90-day-plus gold-loan overdues at 0.3% in August, up from 0.2% in March ([Economic Times](https://m.economictimes.com/industry/banking/finance/whats-under-all-that-glitter-glare-falls-on-booming-gold-loan-business-gold-loan-interest-rate-gold-prices/amp_articleshow/135800635.cms)). Manappuram's Q2 profit rose to ₹701 cr consolidated, but its shares still fell 4.64% on the week ([NSE filing](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/MANAPPURAM_12112026164223_MAFILOUTCOMEFINAL.pdf), [NSE bhavcopy 13 Nov](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/products/content/sec_bhavdata_full_13112026.csv)).
- **The collateral lost about 4% in a week.** Spot gold had its worst week since early June, down about 4.5% to $3,879.71 ([Mint/Reuters](https://www.livemint.com/market/ratehike-bets-keep-gold-on-track-for-worst-week-in-four-months-11794598496469.html)). IBJA 999 fell 3.99% to ₹1,35,809 per 10 g between the 6 Nov and 13 Nov PM rates, and AGLOC cut its 85% LTV ceiling three times, from ₹11,013/g to ₹10,574/g for 14–16 Nov ([IBJA](https://ibjarates.com/), [AGLOC](https://www.agloc.org/)).
- **Rates turned back up.** October CPI came in at 6.09%, above RBI's 6% upper band, with food at 8.94% ([MoSPI](https://www.mospi.gov.in/uploads/latestReleases/latest_release_1794478693814_7c90e80f-9e64-4aa4-b44a-1dc727b0fed9_Press_Release_of_CPI_for_October_2026_.pdf)). The 10-year G-sec rose 12 bps on the week to 7.3079%, giving back about half of the previous week's fall, and the 1-year OIS ended at 6.50% ([ET/Reuters](https://m.economictimes.com/markets/bonds/india-10-year-bond-yield-reverses-half-of-last-weeks-drop-on-elevated-inflation/amp_articleshow/135804127.cms)). Markets expect a 25 bp repo hike to 5.75% at the 2–4 Dec MPC ([BusinessLine](https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/money-and-banking/g-sec-yields-harden-as-oct-inflation-breaches-6-mark-us-yields-rise/article71698427.ece)).
- **Competitors raised equity, and RBI may limit who can control them.** IIFL Finance's board approved a ₹6,414 cr preferential issue led by ₹5,000 cr from Blackstone ([ET](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/iifl-finance-to-raise-rs-6414-crore-through-preferential-issue-blackstone-to-invest-rs-5000-crore/articleshow/135711113.cms)). Bajaj Finance allotted ₹5,799 cr of warrants to its promoter and opened an ₹11,700 cr QIP ([NSE filing](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/BAJFINANCE_11112026171309_SEintimationopeningofissue.pdf)). Reuters reported that RBI is drafting rules to stop one private equity firm controlling more than one NBFC ([Mint/Reuters](https://www.livemint.com/industry/banking/india-plans-curbs-on-private-equity-ownership-of-nbfcs-report-11794472084478.html)).

**Threads this week.** Eighteen threads had updates between 9 and 15 Nov, not counting the daily market and gold-price trackers. Muthoot Fincorp's Q2 results thread moved from "not on the investor page" on 15 Nov to the BSE filing of 14 Nov evening and ET's report on 15 Nov. The Tranche I NCD thread reached listing on BSE on 11 Nov; the final allotted amount is still not in a published source. The Muthoot Fincorp IPO thread added BusinessLine's DRHP funding numbers and Muthoot Microfin's 19 Nov board meeting on audited half-year accounts for Muthoot Fincorp's restated financials. The gold-loan asset-quality thread and Manappuram's Q2 thread carried the Stage 2 story. IIFL's raise went from a press report to a board approval and a 4 Dec EGM; Bajaj Finance's raise moved to a QIP. New this week: RBI's reported PE-control curbs, October CPI, CII's gold risk-weight ask, Aditya Birla Capital's gold branches and Aye Finance's upgrade.

## 🏛️ Regulatory & Policy Watch

RBI issued nothing addressed to NBFCs this week. Its notifications feed ends with the 11 Nov Domestic Money Transfer Directions for banks and payment operators ([RBI notifications](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx)). What mattered came from a press report and a price index.

**1. RBI is reportedly drafting curbs on private equity control of NBFCs (Reuters, 12 Nov).** Two people told Reuters that RBI wants to stop one private equity firm holding a controlling stake in more than one NBFC, with holdings of 15% or less treated as financial investments under lighter scrutiny. A draft would go out for consultation first, and the rules could come early next year; RBI did not comment ([Mint/Reuters](https://www.livemint.com/industry/banking/india-plans-curbs-on-private-equity-ownership-of-nbfcs-report-11794472084478.html), [ET/Reuters](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/finance/rbi-plans-curbs-on-private-equity-firms-controlling-stakes-in-multiple-non-bank-lenders-report/articleshow/135763029.cms)).
- *Direct impact:* none until RBI publishes a draft.
- *Second order:* it came out the same week IIFL agreed to sell about 16% to Blackstone and Mint listed Bain's 18% of Manappuram among recent foreign stakes ([Mint](https://www.livemint.com/industry/banking/from-banks-to-nbfcs-foreign-capital-chases-india-s-credit-growth-11794389152871.html)). Minority stakes of 15% or less stay easy. Control deals get harder for funds that already run a lender.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: none until a draft appears. Minority stakes of 15% or less, the usual size for IPO investors, would sit outside the reported curbs, and RBI's existing prior-approval rule for control or 26%-plus stakes applies either way.

**2. October CPI at 6.09% puts a December hike in play.** MoSPI's provisional print is 6.09% against 5.54% in September, with food inflation at 8.94%, rural 6.63% and urban 5.41% ([MoSPI](https://www.mospi.gov.in/uploads/latestReleases/latest_release_1794478693814_7c90e80f-9e64-4aa4-b44a-1dc727b0fed9_Press_Release_of_CPI_for_October_2026_.pdf)). BusinessLine reports that market players expect a 25 bp hike to 5.75% after October's increase to 5.50% ([BusinessLine](https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/money-and-banking/g-sec-yields-harden-as-oct-inflation-breaches-6-mark-us-yields-rise/article71698427.ece)).
- *Direct impact:* repo-linked bank lines and CP reprice if RBI moves on 4 Dec.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: bank term loans were 39.69% of its borrowings in March 2026, per BusinessLine's reading of the DRHP ([BusinessLine](https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/muthoot-fincorp-diversifies-funding-to-trim-borrowing-cost/article71695055.ece)), and that is the part that reprices first.

**3. RBI's instruments this week were small.** The Domestic Money Transfer Directions, 2026 (RBI/DPSS/2026-27/476, 11 Nov) consolidate rules for banks and payment operators; cash pay-outs stay capped at ₹10,000 a transaction ([RBI](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13752&Mode=0)). RBI refreshed its NBFC FAQ page ("Updated as on November 11, 2026") ([RBI FAQs](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/FAQView.aspx?Id=92)), cancelled Gandhinagar Leasing and Finance's registration ([RBI](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=63949)) and fined One Mobikwik Systems ₹9 lakh, partly for late fraud reporting ([RBI](https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=63973)). SEBI aligned intermediaries' FATCA/CRS reporting with the Income-Tax Rules, 2026 ([SEBI](https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/nov-2026/reporting-requirement-under-foreign-account-tax-compliance-act-fatca-and-common-reporting-standard-crs-revised-through-income-tax-act-2025-read-with-income-tax-rules-2026_105705.html)).
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: no new requirement. The FAQ refresh was not compared line by line with the earlier version, so it is treated here as a restatement unless RBI flags a change.

**4. CII asked for a review of the 100% risk weight on gold loans.** The ask went to the Finance Ministry with easier ECB conditions for NBFCs ([CNBC-TV18](https://www.cnbctv18.com/economy/cii-recommends-regulatory-relaxations-nbfcs-reform-agenda-to-finance-ministry20030393-20030393.htm)). It's an industry proposal; neither RBI nor the government has responded.
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: a lower risk weight would raise its capital adequacy for the same gold book; no regulator has proposed one.

**5. Still open.** Comments on RBI's draft PSL Directions are due on 26 Nov ([RBI](https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=63925)), and SEBI's Credit Risk-o-Meter for debt offer documents starts on 21 Nov ([SEBI](https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/oct-2026/introduction-of-credit-risk-o-meter-as-an-additional-disclosure-mechanism-for-debt-securities_105081.html)). The revolving-credit and Interest Rate Directions drafts are still not final ([RBI drafts](https://rbi.org.in/Scripts/DraftNotificationsGuildelines.aspx)).
Possible impact on Muthoot Fincorp: the Risk-o-Meter would apply to any public NCD tranche it files after 21 Nov under its ₹4,000 cr shelf.

## 💡 Analyst's Take

The week's surface story is that gold lenders had a bad week: gold fell, the Stage 2 numbers came out, and Manappuram dropped almost 5% on a record profit. Underneath, the market is separating two kinds of gold lender. Diversified lenders with access to equity (Bajaj, IIFL, Godrej Capital, and now Aditya Birla and Sammaan opening gold branches) are being paid to grow. The pure gold lenders are being priced on how well their borrowers adjust to monthly payments. Last week's macro tailwind lasted five sessions. CPI at 6.09% and a hot US print took half of it back, and a December hike is now the base case.

Some of the stress is mechanical. A bullet borrower who misses a monthly interest date lands in Stage 2 even with 20 points of LTV cushion. Bajaj's cure rate, about half of its build back in Stage 1 within a quarter, suggests much of it will reverse. The contrarian concern runs the other way. The bureau data show loan counts down 15% while value rose 12%, so tickets are getting bigger, and Macquarie says some lenders lend to borrowers already overdue elsewhere. Bigger tickets, falling gold and a new payment habit make a worse mix than any one of them alone. Muthoot Fincorp's 1.07% Stage III headline will read well against Manappuram's 1.80%. The question analysts will ask is what its Stage 2 did, and the filing's ratio annexure doesn't say.

cards.title: Muthoot Fincorp Q2 FY27: profit doubles to ₹779 crore, Stage III at 1.07%
cards.summary: Muthoot Fincorp's board approved its unaudited standalone results on Saturday 14 Nov and filed them with BSE that evening: Q2 FY27 profit was ₹779.41 crore against ₹388.31 crore a year earlier and ₹705.48 crore in Q1, on total income of ₹3,408.34 crore (up 70.7% year on year). Loans stood at ₹54,685.50 crore on 30 September, up 19.3% from 31 March, with Stage III at 1.07% of gross loans, net Stage III at 0.63%, provision coverage at 42.01% and capital adequacy at 19.38%.
cards.impact: the gross Stage III ratio sits well below the latest standalone prints of Manappuram (1.8%) and Muthoot Finance (3.87%), while impairment charges rose to ₹183.00 crore from ₹106.21 crore a year ago and ₹93.81 crore in Q1, and finance costs rose 68.7% to ₹1,161.53 crore. The same board meeting recommended converting 40 crore compulsorily convertible cumulative preference shares (CCCPS) into equity and reappointing Thomas John Muthoot, Thomas George Muthoot and Thomas Muthoot…

cards.title: RBI deputy governor rules out easing the 50% FOIR cap for microfinance
cards.summary: In a speech at an MFIN event in Mumbai on 13 Nov, published by RBI on 15 Nov, Deputy Governor Shirish Chandra Murmu turned down the industry's request to count only the interest part of some loans in the 50% repayment-to-income (FOIR) cap, saying it would "tinker with the sanctity of the limit and understate household leverage". He said RBI would review the ₹3 lakh household-income threshold, flagged rising microfinance lending rates and ticket sizes, and said credit…
cards.impact: the cap governs Muthoot Microfin's book and any microfinance-type lending in the group, so there is no relief on household indebtedness limits. The bureau clean-up means microfinance loans reported under the consumer segment will start showing up in microfinance FOIR checks.

cards.title: NBFCs flag 5–15 bps more on funding costs after October's repo hike
cards.summary: ETBFSI's review of Q2 commentary says Aditya Birla Finance expects incremental borrowing costs to rise another 5–10 bps in Q3 and Cholamandalam guides for a 10–15 bps rise for FY27, while Bajaj Finance's CFO flagged a marginal extra margin headwind. Muthoot Finance put its cost of borrowing at about 8.6% on 30 September, with CFO Oommen Mammen saying other issuers were raising bonds at 8.3–8.4%, against about 7.5% earlier.
cards.impact: Muthoot Fincorp's own Q2 finance costs rose 68.7% year on year to ₹1,161.53 crore, ahead of its 19.3% loan growth since March, so the repo hike's pass-through to fresh NCDs and bank lines is the margin line to watch in H2.

cards.title: India Ratings affirms IIFL Finance at IND AA/Stable

cards.impact: IIFL Finance, a gold-loan peer, now sits at the same AA level as Muthoot Fincorp's CRISIL rating, as both compete for retail and institutional NCD money this quarter.

cards.title: Sammaan Capital to enter gold loans in 16 branches this quarter
cards.summary: IHC-backed Sammaan Capital will soft-launch gold loans in about 16 branches in Q3 FY27 and another 30 in Q4, with an indicative ticket of about ₹2 lakh, yields of 11–13%, tenures up to three years and LTV up to 85% below ₹2.5 lakh, its management said on the Q2 call. It joins Tata Capital, Aditya Birla Finance and Godrej Finance among large diversified lenders moving into gold loans.
cards.impact: one more well-funded entrant in Muthoot Fincorp's core product, though its chief operating officer said gold branches take 12–18 months to break even, so the competitive effect is slow.

cards.title: Macro Context
cards.summary: Inflation and rates: CPI at 6.09% with food at 8.94% (MoSPI). Swap rates rose 13–17 bps on the week, and the government sold ₹34,000 cr of the benchmark 2036 bond at a 7.3203% cut-off (ET/Reuters, BusinessLine). - US: October CPI rose 0.4% on the month against a 0.3% forecast (Mint/Reuters); the US 10-year yield ended near 5.12%, up 26 bps for the week, with markets pricing a December Fed hike (ET/Reuters).

cards.title: Analyst's Take
cards.summary: The week's surface story is that gold lenders had a bad week: gold fell, the Stage 2 numbers came out, and Manappuram dropped almost 5% on a record profit. Underneath, the market is separating two kinds of gold lender.
